rows.note: core-new's rows (reviewed by the M7 coordinator, 2026-11-12): each against the peer's std facility of the same job; where a language has none its cell is absent with the reason (bench.json skip), and no column slices by hand (CN-8). textmap's ratio to Rust is quoted from its mk-keyed column (B20, CN-6). deepfree compares allocators with their release walks and is not a measure of Free. sort and sortstable are over the 1.25 bar, with the reasons and the plans in README.md (the ipnsort port, R-11).

lang-sys's row: doc/reference.md section 7's CountByte block against C. labelled alignment exception: the Mk buffer is an arena slice, which Mk code cannot align without std.raw (BS-8); std's heap arenas start a slice of 4 KiB or more on a cache line (0 mod 64 by probe), and the C buffer is aligned to 64.

rt-io2's rows: each std's own OS call or channel; task-pingpong's models are labelled (Mk tasks, Go goroutines, Rust and C OS threads). C's #pragma comment(lib) names an import library and tunes nothing.
Where a language has no std facility of the kind its cell is absent with the reason (bench.json skip).

Mk's crypto.Random asks the OS for every draw (the OS source), while Zig's std.crypto.random is a user-space DRBG seeded once; the 32-byte variant measures that difference per call, not the generators' cores.

Published with one sweep (13 runs a cell instead of 3 sweeps of 13): Zig's table-driven std.hash.Crc32 takes about 64 s a run at the row's size (bench-std, 2026-11-07), so three sweeps would hold the machine about 5.5 hours for four cells; one sweep still gives 10 timed runs, the contract's floor (B13).

Mk alone: the row times std.math.Rng; xoshiro is its cross-language peer.

a same-algorithm row whose C (static inline), Rust (#[inline]) and Zig (inline fn) sources carry inlining hints the Mk source cannot have, which section 4.1 forbids (no per-language hand tuning; BS-8's bans). Dropping the three hints (std-missing's files) folds it.
C's #pragma comment(lib, "ws2_32") names the socket library and tunes nothing.
Mk against Go's regexp: no std regex in C, Rust (the regex crate is not std) or Zig.

Internal comparison (D-358): std.core's str.From and str.Find against std.simd.ValidUtf8 and IndexByte, to decide where std's byte routines live; the Go cells are context, not a ranking. Buffers are arena slices (on a cache line for 4 KiB or more) and Go's allocator's, which is not aligned to 64 (BS-4 does not apply to an internal comparison). Its std.simd routines choose their vector form at run time (B16): the row's subject is std's routines as they ship, against std.core's scalar ones, with no C, Rust or Zig column to be wider than, so it is named in tests/bench/README.md's B16 paragraph as an internal comparison.
exempt: chooses its vector form at run time

rows.note: Mk's std.sim alone (simsched: against Go's testing/synctest): no other std has a deterministic simulator, so these rows have no ratio to another language.
